household.name: The Example Family
household.headline: Your Family · Your City
household.who: a family of 4 (2 adults, 2 young kids with low spice tolerance)

seasonal_produce.winter: winter squash, kale, cabbage, carrots, parsnips, storage apples
seasonal_produce.spring: asparagus, peas, spinach, radishes, spring onions, rhubarb
seasonal_produce.summer: zucchini, corn, tomatoes, peppers, cucumbers, berries, green beans
seasonal_produce.fall: butternut squash, sweet potatoes, apples, pears, Brussels sprouts, cauliflower

hard_rules: NO fish or seafood of any kind
Low spice — kid-friendly heat levels only
preferences: Lower-carb emphasis — minimize rice, pasta, bread, potatoes as main components; replace with vegetables, cauliflower rice, zucchini noodles, or lettuce wraps
Simple and quick — weeknight dinners under 30-40 min active time, minimal complex techniques

budget.notes: Prioritize value proteins and simple ingredients.

special_rules: Incorporate the slow cooker on 1-2 weeknights (include a morning prep note)

stores.label: Costco
stores.strategy: Anchor the week around 1-2 large proteins (whole chickens, bulk chicken thighs, 3lb+ ground beef, pork shoulder) that stretch across multiple meals or provide planned leftovers.

stores.label: Trader Joe's
stores.strategy: Use for affordable produce, pre-made sauces, and quick weeknight shortcuts.

stores.label: Whole Foods
stores.strategy: Flag items where the store brand (365) meaningfully cuts cost vs. name brand.

stores.label: Local Grocery
stores.strategy: Prioritize weekly loss-leader categories — dairy, deli proteins, and pantry staples rotate on predictable sale cycles.

branding.email_subject: 🍽️ Your Weekly Meal Plan — Week of {week_of}
branding.footer: Generated for you every week · Happy cooking 🍽️

podcast.title: Our Dinner Plan
podcast.author: Meal Planner Bot
podcast.description: A few minutes each week walking through the coming week's dinners: what's cooking each night and one quick tip per meal.

hosts.name: Robin
hosts.persona: the host. A warm, dry, quick-witted home cook who talks like a friend coaching you through the week, not an announcer.
hosts.delivery: Calm, low-key, conversational. Quiet confidence, gentle dry humor. Medium-low energy; never announce or sound like an ad. Unhurried pace with natural pauses.

hosts.name: Pip
hosts.persona: the kid co-host. Curious, a little skeptical, funny; asks the question a kid would ask and reacts honestly. Never bratty.
hosts.delivery: A kid around ten. Light, slightly higher voice; simple direct phrasing; curious, sometimes deadpan. A touch faster than an adult. Never a grown-up doing a kid voice.
